title: Ukrainian center Kate Koval details leaving LSU after recruitment of Russian player
content:
LSU center Kate Koval, who is from Ukraine, said on Wednesday her decision to leave the program is based on the Tigers recruiting a Russian player at her position. Last week, coach Kim Mulkey said the 6-foot-5 center was leaving for “personal decisions” but alluded to the signing of Anna Minaeva, who has played for a pro club in Moscow.

Koval’s father serves in the Ukrainian military, which has been at war since Russia’s 2022 invasion.

Mulkey’s decision to sign Minaeva and timing in informing Koval “ultimately made me question whether LSU remained the right place for me,” Koval said in a social media post on Wednesday. She said she was informed “several days” after the transfer portal window closed on April 20.

“For me, this war is not distant or abstract,” Koval’s social media statement read. “People close to me have been killed and wounded in Russian attacks, and places where I grew up and first began playing basketball have been destroyed by missile strikes.”

Midyear NCAA transfers are not eligible to compete immediately at another school if they have been enrolled at an NCAA school during the first academic term, even if they didn’t compete at their original school in that window. LSU’s 2026-27 academic year began on Aug. 24,so Koval would need NCAA approval to become eligible immediately elsewhere.

Koval’s statement appealed to the NCAA to consider her unique circumstances. “More than anything, I hope I am given the opportunity to compete at another school during the 2026-27 basketball season,” her statement concluded. She has at least two years of college eligibility remaining and is eligible for the 2028 WNBA Draft.

Koval, who moved to the U.S. for high school basketball, transferred to LSU from Notre Dame for the 2025-26 season. She averaged 8.3 points and 6.3 rebounds last season. With the transfer of Amiya Joyner, Koval — a 17-game starter for the Tigers — was expected to play a significant role this coming season.

Mulkey said she had a “long talk” with Koval about what she characterized as a “hard decision” for the center.

“I know it is hard because she loves LSU,” Mulkey said last week in a statement. “Kate is a great person. She has to do what she feels is right for her, and we fully support her in that. We all wish her the best.”’

Mulkey told the The New Orleans Advocate that she and Koval talked outside of Koval’s apartment complex about the program’s pursuits of Minaeva, but she said she could not recall when this conversation took place.

She said she would not decline recruiting a player who can help improve her program “because of a conflict.”

“I want you to understand I’m not here to ask you to change how you feel about Russia,” Mulkey told the outlet she said to Koval. “I’m just here out of respect for your family and out of respect for you to let you know. Because I know how personal it is for you.”

Koval said her decision to leave LSU was difficult.

“While I understand and respect that roster decisions are a part of college basketball,” her statement said, “I have to remain true to myself, my values and my country.”
